title: India's First Caste Census Since 1931 Just Cleared Its Last Legal Hurdle. The Diaspora Debate Is About to Get Louder.
excerpt: The Supreme Court dismissed a challenge to caste enumeration in the 2027 census, ruling it a policy matter. For NRIs already divided over caste-based reservations, the most comprehensive count in nearly a century will rewrite the argument.
body:
The Supreme Court of India on Wednesday dismissed a public interest litigation challenging the government's decision to include caste enumeration in the upcoming 2027 population census — clearing the last significant legal obstacle to what will be India's most comprehensive caste count in nearly a century.

A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant was unequivocal. "Whether the census should be caste-based or not is a policy decision," the court said. "The government must know how many persons are in the backward castes, what kind of welfare measures are to be taken for them. It is within the policy domain." The PIL, filed by Sudhakar Gummula, was dismissed in minutes.

## Why 1931 Matters

The last time India counted its population by caste was under British colonial rule, in the 1931 census. Every census since independence — from 1951 through the pandemic-delayed exercise now underway — has recorded religion and tribe but not caste. The deliberate omission reflected a post-independence consensus, championed by Jawaharlal Nehru, that enumerating caste would entrench the very divisions India was trying to dismantle.

That consensus has eroded. The demand for a caste census has grown steadily louder over the past decade, driven by parties representing Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Dalit communities who argue that without accurate data, the government is designing welfare programmes — and calibrating reservation quotas — in the dark. Bihar conducted its own state-level caste survey in 2023, which revealed that OBCs and Extremely Backward Classes together constituted over 63 percent of the state's population, far exceeding the quota allocations they received.

## The 2027 Census: Scale and Stakes

The 2027 census — officially India's 16th — is already the most ambitious data-gathering exercise in human history. It will enumerate over 1.4 billion people across two phases: house-listing from April to September 2026, and population enumeration beginning February 2027. It will be India's first fully digital census, with self-enumeration available through a mobile application.

Adding caste to this exercise transforms it from a demographic headcount into a political instrument of enormous power. Accurate caste data will provide the empirical foundation for re-evaluating reservation policies, redistributing welfare spending, and — most controversially — potentially redrawing the boundaries of who qualifies as "backward" and who does not.

The political fault lines are stark. The BJP government, which authorized the caste enumeration after years of resistance, appears to have calculated that the data will strengthen its outreach to OBC voters — a constituency critical to its electoral dominance. The opposition, led by the Congress party's Rahul Gandhi, had made the caste census a central demand and now faces the awkward position of seeing the ruling party deliver it.

## The Diaspora Dimension

For the Indian diaspora, the caste census arrives at a moment when caste has become one of the most contested identity markers in Western public life. California's caste discrimination bill, signed into law in 2023, made the state the first jurisdiction outside South Asia to explicitly ban caste-based discrimination. Universities including Harvard and Princeton have added caste to their non-discrimination policies. Corporate diversity programmes at Google, Apple, and Cisco have grappled with caste complaints from Indian-origin employees.

The diaspora is deeply divided. Many upper-caste NRIs view the census and the broader caste discourse as an attempt to transplant India's reservation politics onto communities that have moved beyond those categories. Dalit and OBC diaspora groups counter that caste discrimination persists in professional networks, temple governance, marriage markets, and social hierarchies abroad — and that data is the first step toward acknowledgment.

The 2027 census will hand both sides ammunition. If the data reveals that backward castes constitute a significantly larger share of the population than current quotas account for, the pressure to expand reservations will intensify — including demands for sub-categorization within the existing OBC quota. If the data shows caste categories are more fluid than assumed, it could complicate the very framework that reservations rest upon.

## What Comes Next

The house-listing phase is already underway. Enumerators will record caste alongside religion, language, education, occupation, and economic status, building the most granular portrait of Indian society ever assembled. The data, once released, will be parsed by political parties, courts, activists, economists, and — inevitably — by the 18 million Indians scattered across the world who remain invested in the question of what India owes to whom.

The Supreme Court's dismissal on Wednesday was brief, but its implications are not. For the first time in 96 years, India will know, with statistical precision, what its caste structure looks like. What it does with that knowledge will define the next generation of Indian politics — and the next chapter of the diaspora's relationship with home.
